definition: Insulated means shielded or protected from outside influences or pressures.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word insulated. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know insulated should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Palace advisers kept the young king insulated from every piece of bad news, so the famine caught him entirely by surprise.
A cushioned fall still lands — the impact is only softened; insulated goes further, keeping the pressure from being felt at all.
Cocooned outdoes insulated: an insulated firm still trades in the open market with one pressure blocked, while a cocooned heir floats sealed away from the world entirely.

Shielded means actively defended — something stands between you and a blow, like a bodyguard or a legal team, usually against a visible attack. Insulated is quieter and more constant: a layer keeps the pressure from ever being felt, the way thick walls keep out cold.

Immune means the pressure can land on you and still do no harm — the body itself shrugs it off. Insulated means the pressure never reaches you at all: a barrier holds it away, and if the barrier comes down you can be hurt again.

Insulated means shielded or protected from outside influences or pressures.
The star quarterback has never read his own press.
His coaches screen every interview request, an assistant filters his mail, and teammates have standing orders not to repeat what the radio shows say.
Insulated from a decade of criticism, he plays with a rookie's easy confidence — and, his critics grumble, a rookie's blind spots.
Insulated fits better than sheltered because it names a barrier kept up on purpose against a specific pressure — criticism — rather than a general softness of upbringing.
And it is not insular: the quarterback's team studies every rival's film hungrily; only the noise is kept out.
Insulated is for protection from pressures: markets, criticism, bad news, cold.

It shares its island root with this unit's insular, but the two judge differently — insulated describes a shield someone or something provides, and can be lucky or dangerous, while insular accuses a group of sealing its own mind.
A senator can be insulated from donors yet never insular in her reading.

The frost came early that year, hard enough to blacken the fields by the second week of October.
Inside the botanical garden's glasshouse, though, the orchids never noticed.
Double panes, heated pipes along the floor, and a curtain of warm air at the door kept the collection insulated from a winter that was punishing everything outside.
The head gardener liked to point out that the flowers were not tough — they were protected.
Move one orchid past the threshold, she said, and the cold would kill it in an hour.
Protection like that is quiet work: no drama, no rescue, just a standing barrier doing its job every hour of the season.
